sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the clip states the construct was made and used in experiments but reports no specific surface-expression or functional assay result for the tagged protein.
sites.rationale: EFNA1 is GPI-anchored (topology: all-O from residue 19 to 205, no M or I residues), so the C-terminus is covalently attached to the GPI lipid anchor and is not accessible for surface tagging. The mature N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage (junction 18|19, A|D) is therefore the sole extracellular terminus and the only position consistent with a full-length membrane-anchored tagged construct. The YFP fusion reported in L2 must reside here by elimination; insert_after_residue=18 is computed from the signal-peptide landmark (residues 1–18), not chosen arbitrarily. Full-length human YFP-tagged ephrin-A1 was engineered and used in cell-based experiments (PMC7957476). EFNA1 is a GPI-anchored protein with no transmembrane or intracellular domain; the mature N-terminus (residue 19, after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 18) is the only free extracellular terminus available for tagging.

sources.claim: Human YFP-tagged ephrin-A1 was constructed as previously described [ 19 ].

literature_notes: L1 (PMC7957476) was evaluated and rejected: the pcDNA3.1 construct covers residues 19–174, which omits the GPI-anchor signal sequence (approximately residues 175–205). A construct lacking the GPI signal is secreted as a soluble ectodomain rather than membrane-anchored, disqualifying it under the rule excluding soluble ectodomain constructs. The GST-fusion arm of L1 (19–205 in pGEX6P-1) is a prokaryotic soluble fusion and likewise excluded. L2 names no residue; because EFNA1 has no TM helix and no intracellular domain, exactly one extracellular terminus exists (the mature N-terminus at residue 19), making the position topology-derived rather than inferred. YFP (~239 aa) is larger than the target short epitope tag, but the fusion precedent supports the junction as tolerant of an N-terminal appendage; a short ALFA or similar tag at the same position is the intended application.
